title: Integer `modulus`: zero divisor and sign
description: Native, except `MIN % -1`. `%` raises on zero and truncates (`-7 % 2 = -1`, `7 % -2 = 1`), as Lean does, so `division_type` makes no difference between the two. But `MIN % -1` raises `Overflow in division`, where the reference gives 0 (found by the probes, duckdb-R15-int-modulus), so the SQL writes that case out.
If the reference picks `FLOOR`, DuckDB needs a shim, `x % y + CASE WHEN x % y <> 0 AND (x % y < 0) <> (y < 0) THEN y ELSE 0 END`. With `error_on_division_by_zero` off, the guard of duckdb-R2.
reference: Substrait and the reference: `modulus` on integers raises on a zero divisor (the decided default for division by zero). Its `division_type: [TRUNCATE, FLOOR]`, the remainder's sign, is open. The parser accepts an explicit `TRUNCATE`, which is what it models, and refuses `FLOOR`.
Lean: no finding. `verify` reports `division by zero` as an error. The remainder truncates (`Int.tmod`).

provenance.notes: `MIN % -1` raises. `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).
